If the rating system penalises drivers who refuse unsafe deliveries, the low ratings are caused by the firm's own rules, not by poor service, which supports changing the system. The drivers being independent contractors is a legal classification, not a reason to keep an unfair rating. Customers liking fast delivery is a preference, not evidence the rating is fair. A rival using a similar system does not make this one fair. The platform being popular does not show the rating is just.
options: The rating system penalises drivers who refuse deliveries that would require speeding or breaking traffic rules
The drivers are independent contractors, not employees of the platform
Customers like fast delivery and give low ratings to slow drivers
A rival platform uses a similar rating system
The platform is the most popular food delivery app in the city
items.passage: A food delivery platform rates its 8,000 riders on a five-star scale based on customer ratings, delivery time and order acceptance rate. Riders who fall below 4.2 stars lose access to the best delivery slots and earn 30 percent less, and riders below 3.8 stars are removed from the platform. Riders complain that the rating is unfair: customers give low ratings for late deliveries caused by traffic or by restaurants that are slow to prepare food, and the acceptance rate penalises riders who refuse orders that would require them to ride dangerously fast. The platform's operations head argues that the rating system keeps quality high, that customers have the right to rate, and that removing low-rated riders protects the brand. The rider welfare head argues that the system punishes riders for factors outside their control, that it pushes riders to break traffic rules to keep their rating, and that it should be changed to measure only what riders control. The chief executive must decide before the festive season, when order volumes double and rider earnings are at their highest. The festive season starts in four weeks, when order volumes double and rider earnings are at their highest for the year. Riders who fall below 4.2 stars lose access to the best delivery slots and earn 30 percent less, which is a large sum for people who depend on the platform for their living. The platform has 8,000 riders in the city and its operations head has said the rating system is the main tool for keeping quality high. The rider welfare head has collected 500 complaints about unfair ratings in the last three months.
items.question: Which of the following, if true, would most strongly support changing the rating system?

A month later, the festive season has begun and order volumes have doubled. The rider welfare head has collected 500 complaints about unfair ratings in the last three months. Five facts have come to light. (A) Customers give low ratings for late deliveries caused by traffic or by restaurants that are slow to prepare food, which riders cannot control. (B) Riders below 4.2 stars lose access to the best delivery slots and earn 30 percent less. (C) The rating system keeps quality high, and customers have the right to rate. (D) The acceptance rate penalises riders who refuse orders that would require them to ride dangerously fast. (E) Riders below 3.8 stars are removed from the platform. Which combination of three facts MOST helps the chief executive change the rating so that it measures only what riders control?
options: (A), (B) and (D)
(A), (C) and (E)
(B), (C) and (D)
(A), (B) and (E)
(C), (D) and (E)
items.explanation: Changing the rating is justified by three legs: riders are rated down for delays they cannot control (A), the penalty for a low rating is large, 30 percent less pay (B), and the acceptance rate pushes riders to ride dangerously fast (D). (C) argues for keeping the system, and (E) describes the removal rule without showing why it is unfair. Every distractor triple contains two right facts and one that points the wrong way.

items.question: The rating has been changed to measure only what riders control. The platform now asks for a rule that will stop a rating system from ever again punishing riders for factors outside their control. Which rule best prevents a recurrence?
options: Riders will be rated only by customers, with no review of whether the rating was fair
Riders below 4.2 stars will earn 30 percent less, whatever caused the low rating
The acceptance rate will be kept, so that riders who refuse dangerous orders are penalised
Complaints about ratings will be ignored, because customers have the right to rate

Every factor in a rider's rating must be shown to be within the rider's control, ratings will be reviewed every quarter against complaints, and no rider will lose pay or be removed on a rating alone without a human review
items.explanation: The rule attacks all three causes: uncontrollable factors in the rating, no review of complaints, and automatic pay loss. Rating only by customers with no review repeats the original system, and keeping the acceptance rate repeats the pressure to ride dangerously.

items.passage: An e-commerce platform has discovered that many of its top sellers have bought thousands of five-star reviews from agencies that post fake reviews for a fee. The fake reviews push these sellers to the top of search results, while honest sellers with genuine four-star reviews are buried on later pages. Customers who bought from the top sellers have complained that the products were far worse than the reviews suggested, and a consumer group is threatening to report the platform to the regulator. The platform's trust head wants to remove all fake reviews, ban the sellers who bought them, and publish a clear policy. The commercial head warns that the top sellers generate 40 percent of the platform's revenue, that banning them would cut revenue sharply, and that customers rarely check whether reviews are genuine. The chief executive must decide before the festive sale, when the platform earns a third of its annual revenue and the fake reviews will influence the most purchases. The consumer group has collected 3,000 complaints from customers who bought products that were far worse than the reviews suggested, and it plans to report the platform to the regulator next week. The festive sale starts in three weeks and the platform earns a third of its annual revenue during that period. The top sellers who bought reviews generate 40 percent of the platform's revenue, while honest sellers with genuine four-star reviews are buried on later pages of search results. The trust head has asked for a budget to audit reviews every month. The commercial head has warned that banning the top sellers would cut revenue sharply and could lead to job losses in the sales team.
items.question: Which of the following, if true, would most strongly support the trust head's proposal to remove all fake reviews, ban the sellers who bought them, and publish a clear policy, by showing BOTH that customers have been harmed AND that the regulator is about to act?
options: The top sellers who bought reviews generate 40 percent of the platform's revenue
The consumer group has collected 3,000 complaints from customers who bought products that were far worse than the reviews suggested, and it plans to report the platform to the regulator next week
The festive sale starts in three weeks and the platform earns a third of its annual revenue during that period

The consumer group has collected 3,000 complaints from customers who bought products that were far worse than the reviews suggested, but it has no plan to report the platform and has not set any deadline
The commercial head warns that banning the top sellers would cut revenue sharply and could lead to job losses
items.explanation: The proposal needs two things: evidence that customers have been harmed, and urgency from the regulator. Only the second option gives both: 3,000 complaints from customers who bought products far worse than the reviews suggested, and a plan to report the platform to the regulator next week. The fourth option gives the harm but removes the urgency, since the group has no plan to report. The revenue share and the job losses argue against the ban, and the festive sale argues for delay.

items.question: A week later, the consumer group has said it will report the platform to the regulator next week, and the festive sale starts in three weeks. The chief executive has already ruled out waiting until after the festive sale: the reviews will be dealt with before the sale starts. Five facts have come to light. (A) The audit team believes most of the 28 unproven sellers also bought reviews, judging by sudden five-star spikes. (B) The audit has confirmed bought reviews for only 12 sellers; 28 more are flagged but unproven. (C) Customers who bought from the top sellers have complained that the products were far worse than the reviews suggested. (D) Removing all flagged reviews would also remove genuine reviews from the 28 unproven sellers. (E) The platform earns a third of its annual revenue during the festive sale, when the fake reviews will influence the most purchases. Which combination of three facts MOST helps the chief executive remove only the confirmed fake reviews before the sale, and hold the unproven ones for the audit, rather than removing all flagged reviews at once?
options: (A), (B) and (C)
(A), (B) and (D)
(B), (C) and (D)
(A), (C) and (E)
(B), (C) and (E)
items.explanation: Waiting is already ruled out, so the decision left is about scope, not timing, and that changes which facts matter. The scope facts are (B), only 12 sellers are confirmed and 28 are merely flagged, and (D), removing all flagged reviews would also remove genuine reviews from the 28 unproven sellers. Fact (C) supplies the reason to act now on the confirmed ones: customers have already been misled into buying worse products. Only (B), (C) and (D) covers all three legs. Fact (A) points the wrong way for a narrow removal, since it argues that most of the unproven sellers are guilty too, which is a reason to remove all flagged reviews, so the first, second and fourth options fail. Fact (E) is about timing, and timing is already decided, so the last option leaves the scope question unanswered: it says nothing about what happens to the 28 unproven sellers. The trap is to keep using the timing fact after the timing decision has been made.

items.question: The fake reviews have been removed and the sellers who bought them have been banned. The platform now asks for a rule that will stop fake reviews from ever again deciding search results. Which rule best prevents a recurrence?
options: Sellers will be allowed to buy reviews, provided they buy them from agencies the platform approves
Reviews will be audited every month, sellers found buying reviews will be banned, and search results will rank sellers by verified purchases rather than by review count alone
Reviews will never be audited, because audits cost money and slow down the festive sale
The top sellers will be kept at the top of search results, whatever their reviews say
Customers will be told not to read reviews, because reviews cannot be trusted
items.explanation: Monthly audits, bans and ranking by verified purchases attack all three causes: undetected fake reviews, no penalty for buying them, and search that rewards review count. Allowing approved agencies to sell reviews repeats the deception, and telling customers not to read reviews abandons the system instead of fixing it.

If the airline's own data shows that most passengers book only a week before travel, the last-minute price rise hits the majority, which supports capping it. The airline being profitable and the rival doing the same do not justify the practice. Empty seats being filled at high prices is a revenue gain, not a fairness argument. A regulator inquiry is a risk, not proof of the harm.
options: The airline is profitable and does not need the extra revenue
The airline's own data shows that most passengers on this route book only a week before travel, when the price has already doubled
A rival airline also doubles its prices in the last week
The last-minute seats are mostly bought by business travellers
The regulator has opened an inquiry into airline pricing
items.passage: A domestic airline has introduced dynamic pricing on a popular route, and fares in the last week before departure are now double the price charged three months earlier. The route is used mainly by families visiting relatives and by students returning home, and many passengers have complained that they cannot plan or afford the trip. The airline's revenue head argues that dynamic pricing fills seats efficiently, that passengers who book early pay less, and that the practice is standard across the industry. The customer service head warns that the price rise looks like profiteering, that the airline's brand is built on being affordable for ordinary families, and that a rival airline has kept its prices flat on the same route. The chief executive must decide before the holiday season, when demand on the route triples and the last-week fares will be at their highest. The airline's board is split, and the regulator has asked the airline to explain its pricing. The holiday season starts in six weeks, when demand on the route triples and last-week fares will be at their highest. The route is used mainly by families visiting relatives and by students returning home, many of whom cannot book months in advance. The board is split, with half the directors supporting the revenue head and half supporting the customer service head. The regulator has asked the airline to explain its pricing and has said it may publish the airline's response. A rival airline has kept its prices flat on the same route. The customer service team has received 4,000 complaints about the fare rise in the last month, mostly from families who say they can no longer afford the trip.
items.question: Which of the following, if true, would most strongly support capping the last-week fare increase?

A month later, the holiday season has begun and demand on the route has tripled. The regulator has asked the airline to explain its pricing and has said it may publish the response. Five facts have come to light. (A) The route is used mainly by families visiting relatives and by students returning home, many of whom cannot book months in advance. (B) A rival airline has kept its prices flat on the same route. (C) Dynamic pricing fills seats efficiently, and passengers who book early pay less. (D) The customer service team has received 4,000 complaints about the fare rise in the last month, mostly from families who say they can no longer afford the trip. (E) The airline's board is split, with half the directors supporting the revenue head and half supporting the customer service head. Which combination of three facts MOST helps the chief executive cap last-week fares on this route?
options: (A), (C) and (E)
(B), (C) and (D)
(A), (B) and (E)
(C), (D) and (E)
(A), (B) and (D)
items.explanation: Capping the fare is justified by three legs: the passengers who pay the doubled fare are families and students who cannot book early (A), a rival has kept prices flat, so the airline is losing the argument that the rise is unavoidable (B), and 4,000 complaints show the harm is large and current (D). (C) argues for dynamic pricing, and (E) is about the board's split, which describes the disagreement rather than supporting a cap. Every distractor triple contains two right facts and one that does not support capping.

items.question: The airline has capped last-week fares on the route. The board now asks for a rule that will stop dynamic pricing from ever again doubling the fare for families who cannot book early. Which rule best prevents a recurrence?
options: Fares will be doubled in the last week on every route, because dynamic pricing fills seats efficiently
The airline will stop publishing its fares, so that passengers cannot compare them with the rival's
The regulator will not be told about pricing changes, so that the airline is never asked to explain them

On routes used mainly by families and students, the last-week fare will be capped at a fixed multiple of the three-month fare, and any change to the cap must be published with its reasons before it takes effect
Families will be told to book three months in advance, whatever their circumstances
items.explanation: A cap on the routes where passengers cannot book early, published with reasons, attacks both causes: the doubling itself and the secrecy around it. Doubling on every route repeats the harm, hiding fares repeats the secrecy, and telling families to book early ignores the fact that many cannot.

items.question: A dealer purchases two watches, one for Rs 1200 and one for Rs 800. He marks each 50% above its cost price. He offers a discount of 25% on the first watch and a discount of 10% on the second. What is his overall profit percentage on the two watches together?
items.explanation: The first watch is marked at Rs 1200 x 1.50 = Rs 1800 and sold at Rs 1800 x 0.75 = Rs 1350, a profit of Rs 150. The second is marked at Rs 800 x 1.50 = Rs 1200 and sold at Rs 1200 x 0.90 = Rs 1080, a profit of Rs 280. The total profit is Rs 430 on a total cost of Rs 2000, which is 21.5%. The 12.5% option is the profit on the first watch alone, and the others come from averaging the two discounts instead of weighting by cost.

items.question: Three runners start together from the same point on a circular track of length 1200 metres and run in the same direction at 10 m/s, 8 m/s and 6 m/s. After how many minutes do all three meet again at the starting point for the first time?
options: 10 minutes
8 minutes
12 minutes
6 minutes
15 minutes
items.explanation: The first runner returns to the start every 1200/10 = 120 seconds, the second every 1200/8 = 150 seconds and the third every 1200/6 = 200 seconds. All three are at the start together when the time is a common multiple of 120, 150 and 200, and the smallest such time is 600 seconds, which is 10 minutes. The solver who takes the meeting time of the two fastest runners only, or who divides by the sum of the speeds, gets a planted wrong answer.

items.question: 3 distinct positive integers have an average of 28, and no integer in the set exceeds 70. What is the maximum possible value of the largest integer in the set?
items.explanation: The sum of the 3 integers is 3 times 28, which is 84. To maximise the largest, the other 2 integers must be as small as possible while staying distinct and positive, namely 1 to 2, summing to 3. That alone would give a largest value of 81, but no integer may exceed 70, so the cap binds: the largest value that can actually occur with 2 distinct integers below the cap summing to 84 is 70, and any larger value would force the smaller integers to repeat or to exceed the cap.

items.question: 7 distinct positive integers have an average of 25, and no integer in the set exceeds 90. What is the maximum possible value of the largest integer in the set?
items.explanation: The sum of the 7 integers is 7 times 25, which is 175. To maximise the largest, the other 6 integers must be as small as possible while staying distinct and positive, namely 1 to 6, summing to 21. That alone would give a largest value of 154, but no integer may exceed 90, so the cap binds: the largest value that can actually occur with 6 distinct integers below the cap summing to 175 is 90, and any larger value would force the smaller integers to repeat or to exceed the cap.

items.question: Pipe A can fill a tank in 8 hours while pipe B can empty the full tank in 12 hours. Pipe A is opened at 9 a.m. and pipe B is opened 4 hours later. At what time will the tank be full?
options: 5 p.m. the same day
1 a.m. the next day
9 a.m. the next day
11 p.m. the same day
5 a.m. the next day
items.explanation: Pipe A fills 1/8 of the tank per hour, so in the 4 hours before pipe B opens it fills 4/8, or half the tank. Once pipe B opens, the net fill rate is 1/8 - 1/12 = 1/24 of the tank per hour, so the remaining half takes 1/2 divided by 1/24, which is 12 hours. The tank is full 4 + 12 = 16 hours after 9 a.m., which is 1 a.m. the next day. Ignoring pipe B gives 5 p.m., and using the net rate from the start ignores the 4-hour head start and gives 9 a.m. the next day.

items.question: Two concentric circles have radii such that the inner circle has a circumference of 132 cm and the outer circle has a radius of 28 cm. A square is inscribed in the inner circle. What is the area of the ring between the circles plus the area of the square? (Use pi = 22/7)
items.explanation: The inner radius follows from the circumference: 2 times 22/7 times the radius is 132, so the inner radius is 21 cm. The ring area is 22/7 times (28 squared minus 21 squared), which is 1078 sq cm. The square inscribed in the inner circle has its diagonal equal to the diameter, 42 cm, so its area is 42 squared divided by 2, which is 882 sq cm. The total is 1078 plus 882, which is 1960 sq cm. The 1078 option is the ring alone, and the solver who uses the outer area alone gets a planted wrong answer.

items.question: What is the maximum area of a rectangle that can be inscribed in a semicircle of radius 14 cm, with one side of the rectangle lying on the diameter of the semicircle?
items.explanation: Let the rectangle have half-width x and height h, with x squared plus h squared equal to 14 squared, since the top corners lie on the semicircle. Its area is 2 times x times h, which is largest when x equals h, that is when x is 14 divided by the square root of 2, giving an area of 196 sq cm. The solver who uses the full circle result, twice the radius squared, forgets that only half the circle is available, and the solver who takes the square of side 14 gets a smaller area.

items.question: An isosceles triangle has a base of 16 cm and each of its equal sides is 10 cm long. A rectangle of maximum area is inscribed in the triangle with its base lying on the triangle's base. What is the area of that rectangle?
items.explanation: The altitude of the triangle is found by Pythagoras: the square root of (10 squared minus 8 squared) is 6 cm, so the triangle's area is half of 16 times 6, which is 48 sq cm. Let the rectangle have height h. By similar triangles its base is 16 times (6 minus h) divided by 6, so its area is 16h(6 minus h)/6, which is largest when h is 3 cm, giving a base of 8 cm and an area of 24 sq cm. The maximum rectangle in any triangle has half the triangle's area. The 48 option is the triangle's area, and the solver who takes the rectangle to be half the base by the full height gets 32.

items.question: What is the sum of the areas of the largest square that can be inscribed in a semicircle of radius 16 cm, with one side of the square lying on the diameter of the semicircle, and the largest square that can be inscribed in the full circle of the same radius?
items.explanation: For the semicircle, let the square have side s. Its two upper corners lie on the semicircle, so by Pythagoras s squared plus (s/2) squared equals 16 squared, giving s squared equal to 4 times 256 divided by 5, which is 204.8 sq cm. For the full circle, the largest inscribed square has its diagonal equal to the diameter, 32 cm, so its area is 32 squared divided by 2, which is 512 sq cm. The sum is 204.8 plus 512, which is 716.8 sq cm. The 204.8 option is the semicircle square alone, and 512 is the full-circle square alone.

items.question: A cylinder has a base circumference of 132 cm and a height of 14 cm. A cone of the same base and height is hollowed out of it. What is the volume of the remaining solid? (Use pi = 22/7)
items.explanation: The base radius follows from the circumference: 2 times 22/7 times the radius is 132, so the radius is 21 cm. The cylinder's volume is 22/7 times 21 squared times 14, which is 19404 cubic cm. The cone removed has the same base and height, so its volume is a third of the cylinder's, 6468 cubic cm. The remaining solid is 19404 minus 6468, which is 12936 cubic cm. The 19404 option is the whole cylinder, and the solver who subtracts half the cylinder instead of a third gets a planted wrong answer.

items.question: How many integers from 1 to 200 are divisible by 3 or by 5 but NOT by both?
items.explanation: From 1 to 200, 66 numbers are divisible by 3, 40 are divisible by 5, and 13 are divisible by both, since 13 multiples of 15 lie in the range. The numbers divisible by 3 or 5 total 66 plus 40 minus 13, which is 93. Removing the 13 that are divisible by both leaves 93 minus 13, which is 80. The 93 option counts the union without removing the overlap, and the 66 option counts only the multiples of 3.

items.question: How many four-digit numbers are divisible by 12, 15 and 18, and also divisible by 7?
items.explanation: A number divisible by 12, 15 and 18 is a multiple of their LCM, 180. To also be divisible by 7 it must be a multiple of the LCM of 180 and 7, which is 1260. The four-digit multiples of 1260 are 1260, 2520, 3780, 5040, 6300, 7560 and 8820, which is 7 numbers. The 50 option counts the four-digit multiples of 180 without the extra condition, and the solver who uses the LCM of 12, 15 and 18 only gets that answer.

items.question: What is the largest positive integer n such that n! ends in exactly 24 trailing zeroes?
items.explanation: The number of trailing zeroes in n! is the exponent of 5 in n!, which is n/5 + n/25 + n/125 and so on, taking whole parts. For n = 100 that gives 20 + 4 = 24. Adding 1, 2, 3 or 4 changes nothing, since no new multiple of 5 appears, so 101!, 102!, 103! and 104! also end in 24 trailing zeroes. At n = 105 a new multiple of 5 appears and the count becomes 21 + 4 = 25, so the largest n with exactly 24 trailing zeroes is 104. The solver who stops at 100 misses the four values that share the same count.

items.question: What is the largest integer n such that n squared is less than 2000, n is divisible by 5, n is NOT divisible by 3, and n + 1 is divisible by 7?
items.explanation: The largest integer whose square is less than 2000 is 44. Counting down through the multiples of 5: 40 is not divisible by 3, but 40 plus 1 is 41, which is not divisible by 7. Next 35: 35 plus 1 is 36, which is not divisible by 7. Next 30 is divisible by 3, so it is excluded. Next 25: 25 plus 1 is 26, which is not divisible by 7. Next 20: 20 plus 1 is 21, which is divisible by 7, and 20 is not divisible by 3, so 20 is the answer. The 40 option ignores the extra condition, and the solver who forgets the exclusion takes 30.

items.question: Two numbers p and q satisfy p + q = 10 and p squared + q squared = 58. What is p cubed + q cubed?
items.explanation: The product must be derived before the cubes can be found. From (p + q) squared = p squared + 2pq + q squared, 100 = 58 + 2pq, so pq = 21. Then p cubed + q cubed = (p + q) cubed - 3pq(p + q) = 1000 - 3 x 21 x 10 = 1000 - 630 = 370. Checking directly, p and q are 3 and 7, and 27 + 343 = 370. The 1000 option cubes the sum and forgets the correction term.

items.question: What is the minimum value of (x - 3) squared + (x - 8) squared + (x - 13) squared, where x is an integer?
items.explanation: The sum is minimised near the mean of 3, 8 and 13, which is 8. At x equals 8 the value is 25 plus 0 plus 25, which is 50. At x equals 7 it is 16 plus 1 plus 36, which is 53, and at x equals 9 it is 36 plus 1 plus 16, which is 53, so 50 is the minimum. The solver who minimises only the first two squares, or who takes the value at the midpoint of the outer terms without checking, gets a planted wrong answer.

items.question: A fair coin is tossed 5 times. Given that exactly 3 heads occur, what is the probability that the first toss and the last toss are both heads?
items.explanation: Condition on the given event first: there are C(5,3) = 10 sequences with exactly 3 heads, and these form the new sample space. For the first and last tosses both to be heads, the middle three tosses must contain exactly 1 head, which happens in C(3,1) = 3 ways. The conditional probability is therefore 3/10. The 3/16 option is the unconditional probability that the first toss is a head and exactly 3 heads occur, and the 1/2 option ignores the condition entirely.

items.question: In a survey of 80 people, 20 like only tea, 13 like only coffee, and 12 like both tea and coffee. 30 people in total like juice. Between 8 and 15 people like both juice and at least one of tea and coffee. What is the minimum possible number of people who like none of tea, coffee and juice?
items.explanation: The people who like tea or coffee total 20 plus 13 plus 12, which is 45. Of the 30 who like juice, between 8 and 15 also like tea or coffee, so the number who like juice only is between 15 and 22. The number who like none is 80 minus 45 minus the juice-only count, which is 5 plus the overlap. The overlap is at least 8, so the minimum possible number who like none is 13. The 5 option assumes no overlap at all, and the 20 option uses the maximum overlap instead of the minimum.

items.question: What is the two-digit number? Statement I: The number is a multiple of 11. Statement II: The sum of its digits is 8.
options: Statement I alone is sufficient, but statement II alone is not sufficient.
Statement II alone is sufficient, but statement I alone is not sufficient.
Both statements together are sufficient, but neither statement alone is sufficient.
Either statement alone is sufficient.
Neither statement alone nor both together are sufficient.
items.explanation: Statement I alone leaves nine possibilities: 11, 22, 33, 44, 55, 66, 77, 88 and 99. Statement II alone leaves eight: 17, 26, 35, 44, 53, 62, 71 and 80. Together, only 44 is both a multiple of 11 and has digits summing to 8, so both statements together are sufficient and neither alone is.

items.question: If China's 2024 exports had grown at the same percentage rate as the UAE's 2024 growth over 2023, what would China's 2024 exports have been, in USD billion, rounded to the nearest whole number?

diagram.caption: Exports (USD billion) to five countries, 2023 and 2024

options: USD 52 billion
USD 48 billion
USD 45 billion
USD 41 billion
USD 50 billion
items.explanation: The UAE's exports grew from 22 to 28 billion, a rise of 6 on 22, which is about 27.27 percent. Applying the same rate to China's 2023 exports of 38 billion gives 38 x 1.2727, about 48.36 billion, which rounds to 48 billion. The other options come from using the wrong base year, the wrong country's rate, or no rounding.

items.question: Which country recorded the highest percentage growth in exports from 2023 to 2024?

diagram.caption: Exports (USD billion) to five countries, 2023 and 2024

options: USA
China
UK
UAE
Germany
items.explanation: The growth rates are USA 15.56%, China 7.89%, UAE 27.27%, UK 16.67% and Germany 13.33%, so UAE grew fastest. The USA has the largest absolute increase, but the question asks for percentage growth.

items.question: Which of the following statements CANNOT be true, given the data?

diagram.caption: Exports (USD billion) to five countries, 2023 and 2024

options: USA's total exceeds China's total by 18
If Germany's 2024 exports doubled, Germany's total would exceed the UK's total
The combined total of USA and China exceeds the combined total of the other three countries
UAE's share of the grand total is more than 16 percent
If the UK's 2023 exports had been 10 higher, the UK's total would have exceeded UAE's total
items.explanation: First compute the country totals across both years: USA 97, China 79, UAE 50, UK 39 and Germany 32, giving a grand total of 297. (A) is true because 97 minus 79 is 18. (B) is true because doubling Germany's 2024 figure of 17 raises Germany's total to 49, above the UK's 39. (C) is true because the USA and China together are 176, above the other three together at 121. (D) is true because the UAE's 50 is about 16.8 percent of 297, above 16 percent. (E) is false: adding 10 to the UK's 2023 figure raises the UK's total only to 49, still below the UAE's 50. Only (E) contradicts the figures, so it is the statement that cannot be true.

items.question: By how many percentage points does East's percentage growth in sales from 2024 to 2025 exceed North's percentage growth over the same period?
items.explanation: East sales grow from 90 to 110, an increase of 20 on a starting figure of 90, which is 22.2 percent. North sales grow from 120 to 140, an increase of 20 on a starting figure of 120, which is 16.7 percent. The difference is 22.2 - 16.7 = 5.6 percentage points. The two regions grow by the same 20 crore in absolute terms, so the difference comes entirely from the different starting figures, which is the trap: the 22.2 percent option is East's growth alone, the 4.0 percent option compares East with West instead of North, and the 15.6 percent option compares East with South.

items.question: In which region is the ratio of 2025 sales to 2024 sales the highest?
options: North
South
East
West
North and West together
items.explanation: Compute the 2025 to 2024 ratio for each region: North 140 over 120 is 1.17, South 160 over 150 is 1.07, East 110 over 90 is 1.22, and West 130 over 110 is 1.18. East has the highest ratio, so its sales grew fastest in percentage terms, even though its absolute sales are the smallest. The trap is to pick the region with the largest absolute sales, or the largest absolute increase, rather than the largest ratio.

items.question: What is the overall percentage growth in total sales from 2024 to 2025?
items.explanation: Total sales rose from Rs 470 crore to Rs 540 crore, an increase of Rs 70 crore, which is 14.89%. Averaging the four regional growth rates gives a different figure, which is wrong because the regions have different sizes.

items.question: If Clothing orders rise to 8000 at the same return rate and Electronics orders fall to 3000 at the same return rate, what is the new total number of non-returned orders across all three categories?

diagram.caption: Orders and return rates in three product categories
diagram.content: An e-commerce firm received 4000 orders for Electronics with a return rate of 10%, 6000 orders for Clothing with a return rate of 15%, and 5000 orders for Grocery with a return rate of 5%.

items.explanation: After the change, Electronics has 3000 orders with a return rate of 10 percent, giving 3000 times 0.90, which is 2700 non-returned orders. Clothing has 8000 orders with a return rate of 15 percent, giving 8000 times 0.85, which is 6800. Grocery is unchanged at 5000 times 0.95, which is 4750. The new total is 2700 plus 6800 plus 4750, which is 14250. The 13450 option is the original total without the change, and the solver who applies the new order figures to the wrong categories gets a planted wrong answer.

items.question: If Grocery orders double at the same return rate, which category then has the largest number of returns?

diagram.caption: Orders and return rates in three product categories
diagram.content: An e-commerce firm received 4000 orders for Electronics with a return rate of 10%, 6000 orders for Clothing with a return rate of 15%, and 5000 orders for Grocery with a return rate of 5%.

options: Electronics
Clothing
Grocery
Clothing and Grocery
All three groups have the same number
items.explanation: The returns are Electronics: 4000 times 10 percent, which is 400, Clothing: 6000 times 15 percent, which is 900, and Grocery: 5000 times 5 percent, which is 250. If Grocery orders double to 10000, its returns double to 500, which is still less than Clothing's 900. So Clothing still has the largest number of returns. The solver who answers from the largest order volume alone, or who doubles the rate instead of the orders, gets a planted wrong answer.

items.question: Which of the following statements CANNOT be true, given the data?

diagram.caption: Orders and return rates in three product categories
diagram.content: An e-commerce firm received 4000 orders for Electronics with a return rate of 10%, 6000 orders for Clothing with a return rate of 15%, and 5000 orders for Grocery with a return rate of 5%.

options: The overall return rate is 10.3 percent
Clothing alone accounts for more than half of all returns
If Grocery orders doubled at the same return rate, the overall return rate would fall below 10 percent
The total number of non-returned orders is 13450
Electronics returns exceed Grocery returns by more than 200
items.explanation: The returns are 400, 900 and 250, totalling 1550 out of 15000 orders, an overall return rate of 10.33 percent, so the first statement is true. Clothing accounts for 900 of 1550 returns, which is 58 percent, more than half. If Grocery orders doubled, the totals would be 20000 orders and 1800 returns, a rate of 9 percent, below 10 percent. The non-returned total is 3600 plus 5100 plus 4750, which is 13450. But Electronics returns exceed Grocery returns by 400 minus 250, which is 150, not more than 200, so the last statement cannot be true.

items.question: A briefing states two facts. The 2025 Nobel Prize in Physiology or Medicine was awarded for discoveries concerning peripheral immune tolerance. It was shared by Mary Brunkow, Fred Ramsdell and Shimon Sakaguchi. Which of the following statements is supported by the briefing?
options: Paabo, Julius and Patapoutian shared the 2025 Medicine Nobel for discoveries on peripheral immune tolerance.
Kariko, Weissman and Langer shared the 2025 Medicine Nobel for discoveries on peripheral immune tolerance.
Brunkow, Ramsdell and Sakaguchi shared the 2025 Medicine Nobel for mRNA vaccines.
Brunkow, Ramsdell and Sakaguchi shared the 2025 Medicine Nobel for discoveries on peripheral immune tolerance.
Brunkow and Ramsdell shared the 2025 Medicine Nobel alone, without Sakaguchi.
items.explanation: The trio and the cited field must be matched. The statement naming Brunkow, Ramsdell and Sakaguchi for discoveries on peripheral immune tolerance gets both right. Statements naming trios that won in other years, giving the right trio the wrong cited work, or dropping one member of the trio each fail at least one fact.

items.question: A briefing states two facts. India won the Asia Cup cricket tournament in 2025. India beat Pakistan in the final. Which of the following statements follows from the briefing?
options: Pakistan won the Asia Cup in 2025, beating India in the final.
India won the Asia Cup in 2025, beating Pakistan in the final, so Pakistan were the runners-up.
Sri Lanka won the Asia Cup in 2025, beating Pakistan in the final.
India won the Asia Cup in 2025, beating Bangladesh in the final.
Bangladesh won the Asia Cup in 2025, beating Pakistan in the final.
items.explanation: The winner and the beaten finalist together fix the runner-up. Only the second statement gets the winner, the finalist and the runner-up inference all right. The first and fifth reverse the result, the third names the wrong winner, and the fourth keeps the right winner but names the wrong finalist.

items.question: A briefing states two facts. Donald Trump was sworn in as President of the United States in January 2025. He is the 47th President of the United States. Which of the following statements is supported by the briefing?
options: Joe Biden was sworn in as the 47th President in January 2025.
Kamala Harris was sworn in as the 47th President in January 2025.
Donald Trump was sworn in as the 47th President in January 2025.
Barack Obama was sworn in as the 47th President in January 2025.
Donald Trump was sworn in as the 46th President in January 2025.
items.explanation: The person, the office and the number must all agree. Only the third statement gets all three right. The first, second and fourth name the wrong person, and the fifth keeps the right person but gives him the number of his predecessor, Joe Biden, who was the 46th President.

items.question: A briefing on the 2025 World Test Championship final states two facts. South Africa won the final. The final was played at Lord's in London, where South Africa beat Australia. Which of the following statements follows from the briefing?
options: Australia lost the final at Lord's, so South Africa were champions and Australia runners-up.
South Africa won the final at The Oval.
India won the final.
Australia won the final at Lord's.
The final was played at Lord's but South Africa lost.
items.explanation: The runner-up must be inferred: the side beaten in the final is the runner-up, so Australia finished second. Only the first option combines the winner, the venue and that inference. The second keeps the winner but changes the venue, the third and fourth change the winner, and the fifth keeps the venue but reverses the result.

items.question: A briefing states two facts. At the 71st National Film Awards announced in 2025, Shah Rukh Khan won the Best Actor award for the film Jawan. Jawan was directed by Atlee. Which of the following statements follows from the briefing?
options: Vikrant Massey won Best Actor for Jawan, directed by Atlee.
Ranbir Kapoor won Best Actor for Jawan, directed by Atlee.
Vicky Kaushal won Best Actor for Jawan, directed by Atlee.
Allu Arjun won Best Actor for Jawan, directed by Atlee.
Shah Rukh Khan won Best Actor for Jawan, directed by Atlee.
items.explanation: The actor, the film and the director must all agree. Only the fifth statement gets all three right. The first four name other leading actors of the same period, but none of them won this award for this film, even though the director named beside them is right.

items.question: A briefing states two facts. Divya Deshmukh won the FIDE Women's World Cup in 2025. She beat Koneru Humpy in the final. Which of the following statements follows from the briefing?
options: Divya Deshmukh won the Women's World Cup in 2025, beating Koneru Humpy, so Humpy was the runner-up.
Koneru Humpy won the Women's World Cup in 2025, beating Divya Deshmukh.
Harika Dronavalli won the Women's World Cup in 2025, beating Koneru Humpy.
Divya Deshmukh won the Women's World Cup in 2025, beating Ju Wenjun.
Vaishali Rameshbabu won the Women's World Cup in 2025, beating Koneru Humpy.
items.explanation: The winner and the beaten finalist together fix the runner-up. Only the first statement gets the winner, the finalist and the runner-up inference all right. The second reverses the final, the third and fifth name the wrong winner, and the fourth keeps the right winner but names the wrong finalist.

items.question: A borrower has a home loan whose interest rate is linked to the repo rate and resets every three months. In June 2025 the Reserve Bank of India cut the repo rate to 5.5 percent, a cut of 50 basis points. What follows for the borrower's loan at the next reset?
options: The benchmark for the loan falls by 50 basis points, so the interest rate on the loan falls by the same amount
The benchmark for the loan falls by 25 basis points, so the interest rate falls by half the cut
The interest rate on the loan is unchanged, because the cut applies only to new loans
The interest rate on the loan rises, because a lower repo rate raises bank funding costs
The benchmark for the loan falls to 6.0 percent, so the interest rate falls by 50 basis points from 6.5 percent
items.explanation: The repo rate was cut from 6.0 percent to 5.5 percent, which is 50 basis points, so the benchmark for a repo-linked floating loan falls by the full 50 basis points at the next reset, and the interest rate on the loan falls by the same amount. A floating rate resets to the new benchmark, so the cut is not confined to new loans. A lower repo rate lowers funding costs rather than raising them, so the rate cannot rise. The last option misstates the levels: 6.0 percent was the rate before the cut, not after it.

items.question: A briefing on the 2025 UEFA Champions League final states two facts. Paris Saint-Germain won the tournament. They beat Inter Milan 5-0 in the final. A report says Inter Milan won 5-0. Which correction follows from the briefing?
options: The report is wrong on the winner: Paris Saint-Germain won 5-0, so Inter Milan lost the final by five goals.
The report is right: Inter Milan won 5-0.
The report is wrong on the score: Paris Saint-Germain won 2-0.
The report is wrong: Real Madrid won 5-0.
The report is wrong: Paris Saint-Germain won, but the score was 5-0 to Inter Milan.
items.explanation: The correction must keep the score and reverse the winner: the 5-0 win belongs to Paris Saint-Germain. Only the first option does that. The second accepts the report, the third keeps the winner but changes the score, the fourth names a team that never reached the final, and the fifth contradicts itself by giving the same score to the losing side.

items.question: A briefing states two facts. The COP30 climate summit in November 2025 was held in Brazil. It was held in the city of Belem. Which of the following statements is supported by the briefing?
options: COP30 was held in Egypt, in Belem.
COP30 was held in the United Arab Emirates, in Belem.
COP30 was held in Azerbaijan, in Belem.
COP30 was held in Brazil, in Belem.
COP30 was held in India, in New Delhi.
items.explanation: The country and the city must both be right. Only the fourth statement gets both right. The first three name the host countries of the three previous COP summits, COP27, COP28 and COP29, while keeping the right city, and the fifth names the wrong country and the wrong city.

items.question: A briefing states two facts. Vinod Kumar Shukla was conferred the Jnanpith Award announced in 2025. He is a Hindi writer. Which of the following statements follows from the briefing?
options: Gulzar, a Hindi writer, was conferred the Jnanpith Award announced in 2025.
Amitav Ghosh, a Hindi writer, was conferred the Jnanpith Award announced in 2025.
Damodar Mauzo, a Hindi writer, was conferred the Jnanpith Award announced in 2025.
Krishna Sobti, a Hindi writer, was conferred the Jnanpith Award announced in 2025.
Vinod Kumar Shukla, a Hindi writer, was conferred the Jnanpith Award announced in 2025.
items.explanation: The recipient and the language must both be right. Only the fifth statement gets both right. The other four name other noted Indian writers, but none of them received the Jnanpith announced in 2025, even though the language named beside them is Hindi in each case.

items.question: A briefing states two facts. The Major Dhyan Chand Khel Ratna awards announced in January 2025 included Manu Bhaker. She won two medals at the Paris 2024 Olympics. Which of the following statements is supported by the briefing?
options: Manu Bhaker, a Khel Ratna recipient announced in January 2025, won two medals at the Paris 2024 Olympics.
Neeraj Chopra, a Khel Ratna recipient announced in January 2025, won two medals at the Paris 2024 Olympics.
PV Sindhu, a Khel Ratna recipient announced in January 2025, won two medals at the Paris 2024 Olympics.
Rohit Sharma, a Khel Ratna recipient announced in January 2025, won two medals at the Paris 2024 Olympics.
Manu Bhaker, a Khel Ratna recipient announced in January 2025, won one medal at the Paris 2024 Olympics.
items.explanation: The recipient and the medal count must both be right. Only the first statement gets both right. The second, third and fourth name sportspersons who did not receive this award in this round, and the fifth keeps the right recipient but halves her medal count from two to one.

items.question: A briefing states two facts. The PM Dhan-Dhaanya Krishi Yojana, launched in October 2025, targets the development of 100 districts. The scheme was first announced in the Union Budget 2025-26. Which of the following statements follows from the briefing?
options: The scheme targets 50 districts and was first announced in the Union Budget 2025-26.
The scheme targets 100 districts and was first announced in the Union Budget 2025-26.
The scheme targets 75 districts and was first announced in the Union Budget 2025-26.
The scheme targets 100 districts and was first announced in the Economic Survey 2025.
The scheme targets 200 districts and was first announced in the Union Budget 2025-26.
items.explanation: The number of districts and the announcing document must both be right. Only the second statement gets both right. The first, third and fifth give the wrong district count, and the fourth keeps the right count but names the wrong document, the Economic Survey instead of the Union Budget.

items.question: A briefing states two facts. Jannik Sinner won the men's singles title at Wimbledon in 2025. He also won the Australian Open men's singles title in 2025. Which of the following statements is supported by the briefing?
options: Carlos Alcaraz won Wimbledon in 2025 and also won the Australian Open in 2025.
Novak Djokovic won Wimbledon in 2025 and also won the Australian Open in 2025.
Daniil Medvedev won Wimbledon in 2025 and also won the Australian Open in 2025.
Jannik Sinner won Wimbledon in 2025 and also won the Australian Open in 2025.
Lorenzo Musetti won Wimbledon in 2025 and also won the Australian Open in 2025.
items.explanation: The same player must hold both titles in the same year. Only the fourth statement names the player who won both. The other four name players who won neither of the two titles in 2025, even though the second title named beside them is the right one.

items.question: A briefing on Article 32 states two facts. Dr B.R. Ambedkar described Article 32 as the heart and soul of the Indian Constitution. Habeas Corpus is the writ that produces a person detained illegally before a court, and Article 32 is itself a Fundamental Right. A detainee's family wants the court to order the detained person produced before it. Which writ should they seek, and why does Article 32 matter?
options: Habeas Corpus, because Article 32 is itself a Fundamental Right that lets a person move the Supreme Court directly for enforcement.
Mandamus, because it produces a detained person before a court.
Certiorari, because it produces a detained person before a court.
Quo Warranto, because it produces a detained person before a court.
Habeas Corpus, because Article 32 is only a legal right and not a Fundamental Right.
items.explanation: The writ and the status of the article must both be right: Habeas Corpus produces the detained person, and Article 32 is a Fundamental Right, so the family can move the Supreme Court directly. The second, third and fourth options name writs with different functions, and the fifth names the right writ but gives the wrong reason, since Article 32 is a Fundamental Right.

items.question: A briefing states two facts. G. Sankara Kurup was the first recipient of the Jnanpith Award in 1965. He received it for Odakkuzhal, written in Malayalam. Which of the following statements follows from the briefing?
options: G. Sankara Kurup received the first Jnanpith in 1965 for Odakkuzhal, written in Malayalam.
G. Sankara Kurup received the first Jnanpith in 1965 for Gitanjali, written in Bengali.
G. Sankara Kurup received the first Jnanpith in 1965 for Godan, written in Hindi.
G. Sankara Kurup received the first Jnanpith in 1965 for Kayar, written in Malayalam.
G. Sankara Kurup received the first Jnanpith in 1965 for Chemmeen, written in Malayalam.
items.explanation: The work and its language must both be right. Only the first statement gets both right. The second and third name works by other authors in other languages, and the fourth and fifth name other Malayalam works, Kayar by Thakazhi Sivasankara Pillai and Chemmeen also by Thakazhi, not the prize-winning Odakkuzhal.

items.question: A briefing gives the headquarters of four organisations. World Bank, Washington, D.C. OPEC, Vienna. SAARC, Kathmandu. NATO, Brussels. A delegate flies from the headquarters of the World Bank to the headquarters of NATO. Which cities, in order, does the delegate travel between?
options: Washington, D.C. to Brussels.
Vienna to Brussels.
Washington, D.C. to Vienna.
Kathmandu to Brussels.
Brussels to Washington, D.C.
items.explanation: Two pairings must be read off the briefing and kept in order: the World Bank sits in Washington, D.C. and NATO sits in Brussels. Only the first option gives both cities in the right order. The second starts from the OPEC headquarters, the third ends at the OPEC headquarters, the fourth starts from the SAARC headquarters, and the fifth reverses the direction of travel.

items.question: A briefing gives the publication years of four books. Godan, 1936. Train to Pakistan, 1956. The Guide, 1958. Midnight's Children, 1981. Which of the following statements about their order must be true?
options: The Guide was published before Train to Pakistan.
Godan was the earliest of the four and Midnight's Children was the latest.
Midnight's Children was published before The Guide.
Train to Pakistan was the earliest of the four.
Godan was published after Train to Pakistan.
items.explanation: The years must be ordered: 1936, 1956, 1958 and 1981 put Godan first and Midnight's Children last. Only the second option states that. The first swaps the two middle books, the third moves the latest book before the third, the fourth makes the second book the earliest, and the fifth reverses the first two books.

items.question: A briefing states two facts. Argentina is not a member of BRICS; it declined the invitation to join. Indonesia joined BRICS as a full member in January 2025. Which of the following countries is NOT a member of BRICS as of 2025, and which country joined BRICS as a full member in January 2025?
options: Egypt is not a member, and Indonesia joined in January 2025.
Ethiopia is not a member, and Indonesia joined in January 2025.
Argentina is not a member, and Indonesia joined in January 2025.
Iran is not a member, and Indonesia joined in January 2025.
Argentina is not a member, and Egypt joined in January 2025.
items.explanation: The answer must satisfy two conditions at once: the country named as a non-member must really be outside BRICS, and the joiner must be the January 2025 entrant. Only the third option does both. Egypt, Ethiopia and Iran all joined BRICS in 2024, so the first, second and fourth fail the first condition, and the fifth names the wrong joiner.

items.question: A briefing on Academy Awards states three facts. Satyajit Ray received an honorary Oscar in 1992. Bhanu Athaiya won Best Costume Design for Gandhi in 1983. A.R. Rahman won two Oscars for Slumdog Millionaire in 2009. It also notes that only Ray won the Bharat Ratna, and that Rahman was born in Chennai. Which of the following statements is true of all three?
options: All three won Academy Awards.
All three won the Bharat Ratna.
All three were born in Kolkata.
All three worked with Richard Attenborough.
All three won Oscars for Slumdog Millionaire.
items.explanation: Each claim must be tested against all three people, not just one: each of the three won an Academy Award, so only the first statement holds for all three. The second holds for Ray alone, the third fails for Rahman, who was born in Chennai, the fourth holds for Athaiya alone, who worked on Gandhi, and the fifth holds for Rahman alone.

items.question: A briefing states two facts. Mark Rutte is the Secretary General of NATO as of 2025. He was previously the Prime Minister of the Netherlands. Which of the following statements is supported by the briefing?
options: Jens Stoltenberg is Secretary General of NATO as of 2025, previously Prime Minister of the Netherlands.
Mark Rutte is Secretary General of NATO as of 2025, previously Prime Minister of the Netherlands.
Ursula von der Leyen is Secretary General of NATO as of 2025, previously Prime Minister of the Netherlands.
Antony Blinken is Secretary General of NATO as of 2025, previously Prime Minister of the Netherlands.
Mark Rutte is Secretary General of NATO as of 2025, previously President of the European Commission.
items.explanation: The office holder and his previous role must be matched. Only the second statement gets both right. The first names his predecessor, Stoltenberg, the third and fourth name people who never held the post, and the fifth keeps the right holder but gives him the previous role of the European Commission President.
